claims.text: In-situ induction preheating of the substrate during additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi lowers the thermal gradient between the melt pool and substrate.
Lowering thermal gradients through substrate preheating reduces residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Substrate preheating preserves the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Substrate preheating simplifies additive processing of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional high-thermal-load methods.
Standard high-density-energy-input processing of AlCrFeNiSi causes rapid melting and solidification.
Rapid melting and solidification of AlCrFeNiSi under standard high-density-energy-input processing produces high residual stresses.
Rapid melting and solidification of AlCrFeNiSi under standard high-density-energy-input processing produces phase inhomogeneities.
Rapid melting and solidification of AlCrFeNiSi under standard high-density-energy-input processing degrades mechanical properties.
A substrate temperature of approximately 600–700 °C is an optimized preheating window for additively manufacturing AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing the instantaneous temperature differential between the melt pool and substrate promotes a more equilibrium dendritic or near-equilibrium cellular microstructure.
The promoted dendritic or cellular microstructure decreases excessive dislocation generation.
The promoted dendritic or cellular microstructure minimizes microcrack formation.
A reduced solidification thermal gradient lowers the cooling rate.
Controlled cooling minimizes non-equilibrium microstructures in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Controlled cooling reduces crack formation and distortion.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stresses than components produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have improved ductility relative to components produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will have improved hardness relative to components produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated AlCrFeNiSi components will contain fewer processing-induced defects than components produced without substrate preheating.
